newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products helped by crude, over-supply loom.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products helped by crude, over-supply loom.

text.p: Med oil products were boosted by crude on Monday, traders said, but threatened by over-supply.

Gasoline was steady to slightly up in line with crude gains and higher NYMEX unleaded levels. Traders said demand out of Italy was fairly healthy with the approach of two long weekends at the end of April and beginning of May.
Premium unleaded cargoes for balance of April delivery were talked around $196/$199.
Some players were looking into moving material across to the United States in order to get it out of the area, even though the arbitrage figures are not that favourable at the moment.
Naphtha was slightly higher with crude but trade was quiet. Outright prices were assessed around $175/$179 a tonne cif Med.
Gas oil sellers held out for high prices, but some said the market was longer after a balanced period. The ISAB refinery, restarting in May, will add to the length.

A large 50kt 5-10 May Constanza and a large Skikda parcel were both looking for buyers at high numbers for 5-10 May and 25-30 April dates. Russian material was looking for fob high quotes +$4-4.50, a similar level for Italian 0.2 pct grade.

Demand for cargoes into India remains since the Med was still preferable to the Gulf although current prices wipe out any profit against the majority of India tender awards. Diesel was firmer at fob high EN590 quote +$3.50.
Fuel was again thinly discussed with high sulphur looking long into May. But prices were holding up, mainly because there were no deals to make them anything but notional.
"I expect this week things will go prompt and we'll see a change but right now activity is very thin," a trader said.
Russian straight-runs were not well bid, though the St. Nicholas 2 was finally placed into Italy.
Other Russian cargoes were quietly finding homes as well, dealers added. - London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
